opening_fact.text: I have really bad pain in my right arm.

patient_facts.text: The right arm pain began 3 days ago.
patient_facts.quote: Three days ago.

patient_facts.text: He was playing with his grandchildren in the garden when he tripped and fell.
patient_facts.quote: I was playing with my grandchildren in the garden when I tripped and fell.

patient_facts.text: He stumbled over a toy on the floor, tried to brace himself with his right arm, and ended up landing on his hand.
patient_facts.quote: I stumbled over a toy on the floor and attempted to brace myself with my arm, but I ended up landing on my hand. / he fell on his outstretched right arm
flags: The script does not say which arm he braced with; the side (right) comes from the patient note HPI.

patient_facts.text: Did not lose consciousness.
patient_facts.quote: No.

patient_facts.text: The pain is in the upper and middle parts of the right arm.
patient_facts.quote: The upper and middle parts of my right arm.

patient_facts.text: The arm is not weak.
patient_facts.quote: No, it isn't weak

patient_facts.text: Believes he can move the arm in all directions, but it hurts when he does.
patient_facts.quote: I believe I can move it in all directions, but it hurts when I do.

patient_facts.text: No numbness in the arm.
patient_facts.quote: No numbness.

patient_facts.text: No loss of sensation; he can feel things fine.
patient_facts.quote: I can feel things fine.

patient_facts.text: Felt no pain at the moment he fell.
patient_facts.quote: I didn't feel any pain when I first fell

patient_facts.text: The pain then came on gradually after the fall.
patient_facts.quote: but then the pain started gradually.

patient_facts.text: The pain is stable now but still there.
patient_facts.quote: It is stable now, but it is still there.

patient_facts.text: No pain anywhere else.
patient_facts.quote: No.

patient_facts.text: Has not seen a doctor since the fall 3 days ago.
patient_facts.quote: No.

patient_facts.text: Has used a sling and taken Tylenol for the pain, but the pain improved only slightly.
patient_facts.quote: I utilized a sling and took Tylenol, but the pain only improved slightly.

patient_facts.text: Has also used an ice pack at home.
patient_facts.quote: persisted despite his use of Tylenol and an ice pack at home
flags: Only in the patient note HPI; the scripted answer about measures taken (p011) mentions a sling and Tylenol, not an ice pack.

patient_facts.text: Not moving the arm and Tylenol make the pain better.
patient_facts.quote: Not moving my arm and Tylenol.

patient_facts.text: Using the arm makes the pain worse.
patient_facts.quote: Using my arm.

patient_facts.text: Did not seek care sooner because the pain did not seem that bad and he thought it would get better on its own.
patient_facts.quote: it wasn't that bad, and I thought it would get better on its own
flags: Parser merge: this answer to 'Reason for Not Seeking Medical Attention' sits inside p014's question field (the raw sheet has it on the Doctor line and the doctor's actual question is missing).

patient_facts.text: Did not want to bother his son, who is busy and does not have time to bring him to the hospital.
patient_facts.quote: Also, I didn't want to bother my son. He doesn't have time to bring me to the hospital. He is busy.
flags: Parser merge: this text sits inside p014's question field.

patient_facts.text: Lives with his son in the son's house.
patient_facts.quote: I live with my son in his house.

patient_facts.text: His son is married and has three children.
patient_facts.quote: He is married and has three kids.

patient_facts.text: Life has been hard on his son lately; the son lost his job and is looking for a new one.
patient_facts.quote: Life has been hard on him lately. He lost his job and is looking for a new one.

patient_facts.text: Does not feel unsafe where he lives; says he feels safe.
patient_facts.quote: I feel safe.
flags: Said while looking anxious (stage direction '(looks anxious)'); the gold lists elder abuse as an additional consideration.

patient_facts.text: Says nobody at home bothers him.
patient_facts.quote: Nobody bothers me (looks anxious).
flags: Said while looking anxious; the question asked whether anyone at home hurts or threatens him or whether he is afraid of anyone.

patient_facts.text: Says the people at home are all nice.
patient_facts.quote: They are all nice.

patient_facts.text: Takes Tylenol.
patient_facts.quote: Tylenol

patient_facts.text: Uses an albuterol inhaler.
patient_facts.quote: albuterol inhaler.

patient_facts.text: Allergic to aspirin; it gives him an itchy rash all over his body.
patient_facts.quote: Yes, I am allergic to aspirin. / I get an itchy rash all over my body.

patient_facts.text: Asthma.
patient_facts.quote: I have asthma.

patient_facts.text: Had part of his prostate removed 2 years ago.
patient_facts.quote: They removed part of my prostate 2 years ago.

patient_facts.text: Before the prostate surgery it was very difficult for him to urinate; this has gotten much better since.
patient_facts.quote: It was very difficult for me to urinate, but that has since gotten much better.

patient_facts.text: He was told there was no evidence of cancer in the prostate.
patient_facts.quote: They said there was no evidence of cancer.

patient_facts.text: Retired schoolteacher; no longer works.
patient_facts.quote: I don't work anymore. I am a retired schoolteacher.

patient_facts.text: Does not drink alcohol.
patient_facts.quote: No, I do not consume alcohol.

patient_facts.text: Does not smoke.
patient_facts.quote: No, I don't smoke.

patient_facts.text: Walks 20 minutes every day, to the grocery store and back.
patient_facts.quote: I walk 20 minutes every day to the grocery store and back.

acting_notes: Hold your right arm close to your body with your left hand and keep it externally rotated and slightly abducted.
Express pain when the examiner tries to move your right shoulder in any direction.
Do not allow the examiner to bring your shoulder to its full range of motion in flexion, extension, abduction, or external rotation.
Look anxious when saying that nobody at home bothers you (home-safety questions).
patient_questions: Doctor, do you believe I will regain full movement in my arm as I had before?
I lack insurance coverage. What will the cost be for this appointment?

additional_considerations.rationale: Red flags in the history (anxious behavior, delayed care-seeking) may point to it; abuser and victim often both deny abuse, so the diagnosis is often inferential and supporting evidence must be sought.
Usually nonspecific shoulder pain often referred down the proximal lateral arm, with possible inability to abduct or flex the shoulder and weakness in internal or external rotation.

source_issues: p014 (parser merge): the question field holds the patient's answer to 'Reason for Not Seeking Medical Attention' ("...when it wasn't that bad, and I thought it would get better on its own? Also, I didn't want to bother my son. He doesn't have time to bring me to the hospital. He is busy."), followed by the 'Living Conditions' question. In the raw sheet the answer is written on the Doctor line and the doctor's actual question is missing. The answer field is the Living Conditions answer. Annotated from the correct content (f019-f023), keeping id p014.

p015 (parser merge): the question field joins the 'Social History' question ('Is there anyone else living with you? Do you have a significant other?'), which has no answer in the raw sheet, with the 'Safety/Elder Abuse Screening' question; the answer belongs to the safety question. Whether he has a significant other is unknown.
Note HPI says he used 'Tylenol and an ice pack at home'; the script (p011) says a sling and Tylenol. The ice pack is added as a flagged note-only fact (f016).
Note HPI says he 'fell on his outstretched right arm'; the script says he braced with 'my arm' and landed on his hand without naming the side.

Note PMH lists 'BPH' and PSH 'Prostatectomy'; the patient says only that part of his prostate was removed 2 years ago for difficulty urinating with no evidence of cancer. BPH is a clinician interpretation and was not copied into patient facts.
Note SH: 'Walks for 20 minutes every morning'; script says every day.
Gold diagnosis #1 'pain increases with hand movement': the script describes pain with using or moving the arm, not the hand. Its exam line is one comma-separated sentence, split into three items.
Gold diagnosis #2 exam finding 'Right arm externally rotated and slightly abducted' comes only from the SP notes; the note exam says only 'Right arm held closely against chest wall'.

p006: the patient believes he can move the arm in all directions, while the SP is told not to allow full shoulder range of motion and the note exam records restricted ROM; recorded as the patient's belief.
The sample closure ends with a stray page-number artifact '(203 206)'.
annotator_notes: The home-safety denials (f024, f025) are coded absent and flagged because the script has him look anxious while giving them; the stage direction is kept in acting_notes.

f015 (sling and Tylenol give only slight relief) and f017 (not moving the arm and Tylenol make it better) come from different questions and are both kept; f027 records Tylenol as a current medication.
Prostate history: surgery is historical; the voiding difficulty is historical and 'much better', not explicitly resolved.
The lack of insurance appears only in the challenging question and is kept in patient_questions.
'Sit up in bed' is positioning only and is not an exam finding; the arm position, pain on shoulder movement and restricted ROM are added as sp_notes exam records (x020-x022).
